chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you cast the soil upon the deceased, say: 'In faith in You and affirmation of Your Resurrection, this is what Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) promised us.'

He (peace be upon him) said: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever casts soil upon a deceased and says this statement, Allah will grant him a good deed for every particle (of soil).'
ai.seo_question: What should be said when burying the dead according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith prescribes a specific dhikr affirming belief in the divine promise of resurrection, linking the physical act of burial to spiritual reward. It highlights the Shia tradition of viewing the grave as a transition to the Barzakh, where each grain of earth serves as a vessel for merit, a concept further elaborated by Imam Ali’s narration regarding the multiplicity of rewards for this single act.
